rationale: **Disputed — flagged for the expert.** The fixture files this under 2.5.3 as "a field whose only label is its placeholder", but on the criterion's own terms 2.5.3 is satisfied here: the visible text is the placeholder "Email" and the accessible name computed from that placeholder is "Email", so the name does contain the visible label. The real defects on this element are 3.3.2 (no persistent label — the text vanishes as soon as the user types) and arguably 4.1.2. It is also expected to be never-captured, because the label rule skips a control with no visible text and an <input type="email"> has none. Recorded as a pass under 2.5.3 rather than deleted, so the disagreement is visible and can be adjudicated.
anchor: Understanding SC 2.5.3: Label in Name — applies to components whose labels include text; see also SC 3.3.2

rationale: The button reads "Renew" and its aria-label is "Renew all loans". The name contains the visible text, so the letter of 2.5.3 is met and a voice command matches. But the name widens the scope the visible text promised — "Renew" on its own does not tell a sighted user that pressing it renews every item — so the two audiences are told different things about what the control does. That is a real problem and it is not the one 2.5.3 measures. Uncertain is the calibrated answer.
anchor: Understanding SC 2.5.3: Label in Name — the name must contain, and should begin with, the visible text

rationale: The control reads "Pay charges..." and its accessible name is "Settle outstanding balance", which contains none of the words printed on it. Somebody saying "click Pay charges" — reading the control aloud, which is the whole way speech input is used — matches nothing, because the name the software compares against never contains what is on screen. All eleven controls on this page are rewritten the same way, so no control on the page can be operated by voice. The rewrites are more descriptive than the labels, which is what makes this worth testing: nothing about the page looks like a mistake.

rationale: The same control reading "Pay charges...", named "Pay charges" — the same words without the typographic mark.
